answer: Each bonded identity commits collateral before voting, and signed conflicting messages link coordinated equivocation. If k identities equivocate together, penalties scale with implicated pairs, O(k^2), not linearly. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm, making identity splitting costly; timber, tundra, and cipher are labels, not exemptions from shared evidence rules. Risk therefore follows coordinated behavior, not identity names.
